### The state and a trace-preserving channel

We now combine the two independent inputs to the main state theorem: the operational obstruction for the represented class and the product-free Choi range of the explicit dimension-ten pair.

prerequisites.concept: Independent quadratic evaluations at rank-loss directions

evidence.quote:
#### Local Frobenius and quadratic evaluations

It remains to prove that no nonzero quadratic vanishes on ten of the directions. We will show that the Galois group of the splitting field permutes the twenty roots arbitrarily.

#### The coordinate field and its twenty points

We can now prove independence of the twenty spanning monomials.

### A finite combinatorial realization We construct data satisfying Proposition 26. A restricted-intersection bound gives real unit vectors such that every sufficiently large subfamily contains an orthogonal pair. The fiber argument for threefold tensor products strengthens this conclusion to eight mutually orthogonal members in every sufficiently large subfamily.

outputs.exact_statement: There are explicitly specified PPT maps $\Phi_1,\Phi_2:M_{10}(\mathbb C)\to M_{10}(\mathbb C)$ for which $$Z=J(\Phi_2\circ\Phi_1)$$ is nonzero and its range contains no nonzero product vector in $\mathbb C^{10}\otimes\mathbb C^{10}$. In particular, the composition $\Phi_2\circ\Phi_1$ is not entanglement breaking.
There is an explicitly specified trace-preserving PPT channel $\Theta:M_{21}(\mathbb C)\to M_{21}(\mathbb C)$ whose square $\Theta\circ\Theta$ is not entanglement breaking.

Let $F:M_{a}(\mathbb C)\to M_{b}(\mathbb C)$ be CP. Then $F^\dagger$ and $T_b\circ F\circ T_a$ are CP. Moreover, $$F\circ T_a\text{ is CP}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 T_b\circ F\text{ is CP}.$$ If $F$ is PPT, so are $T_b\circ F$, $F\circ T_a$, its adjoint, its simultaneous transpose $T_b\circ F\circ T_a$, and its transpose-adjoint $F^\sharp:=T_a\circ F^\dagger\circ T_b$. Tensor products of PPT maps are PPT. If $P$ and $Q$ are compatible CP maps, then $Q\circ F\circ P$ is PPT whenever $F$ is PPT.

A linear map $F:M_{a}(\mathbb C)\to M_{b}(\mathbb C)$ is CP if and only if $J(F)\succeq0$. For a CP map, the following are equivalent:*

1.  *$J(F)$ is separable;*

2.  *for every $k\geq1$ and every $W\succeq0$ in $M_{k}(\mathbb C)\otimes M_{a}(\mathbb C)$, $(\mathrm{id}_k\otimes F)(W)$ is separable.*

*Also, $$J(T_b\circ F)=(\mathrm{id}_a\otimes T_b)J(F),\qquad
 J(F\circ T_a)=(T_a\otimes\mathrm{id}_b)J(F).$$
Every nonzero separable positive matrix has a nonzero product vector in its range. Consequently, a nonzero positive matrix whose range contains no nonzero product vector is nonseparable.

The class $\mathscr C$ is closed under finite tensor products, after grouping all first-party systems and all second-party systems. In particular, $\omega^{\otimes n}\in\mathscr C$ for every $\omega\in\mathscr C$ and every $n\geq1$.

Let $H$ and $J$ be square matrices, possibly of different sizes, and let $Z$ have the corresponding rectangular size. If $$\begin{pmatrix}H&Z\\ Z^*&J\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,$$ then $$\left\lVert Z\right\rVert_1\le\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}H\,\operatorname{tr}J}.$$ This estimate includes singular $H$ and $J$.

Let $R$ be a density operator on finite-dimensional complex spaces $A\otimes B$, and let an admitted protocol produce bits $i,j\in\{0,1\}$ almost surely on $R$. Give Eve the canonical purification [eq:canonical-purification], and let her retain $E$ and the complete public transcript $T$ with value $t$ in its standard Borel space $\mathsf T$. There exist a finite positive measure $\mu$ on $\mathsf T$ and measurable positive matrices $X_0(t),X_1(t)$ on $A$ and $Y_0(t),Y_1(t)$ on $B$ such that the positive matrix-valued measure of Eve in bit branch $(i,j)$ has the density $$\label{eq:eve-blocks} \tau_{ij}(t)= \bigl(\sqrt R\,[X_i(t)\otimes Y_j(t)]\sqrt R\bigr)^\mathsf T \quad\text{with respect to }\mu.$$ The same $X_i(t)$ and $Y_j(t)$ work for all four branches outside one $\mu$-null set, and $$\sum_{i,j=0}^1\int_{\mathsf T}\operatorname{tr}\tau_{ij}(t)\,d\mu(t)=1.$$ The transpose in [eq:eve-blocks] is in the product basis identifying $E$ with $A\otimes B$. No invertibility of $R$ is assumed.

Let $R$ and $|\Psi_R\rangle$ be as in Lemma 13, and let $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes B\otimes\widetilde E$ be any purification of $R$. There is a channel $\mathcal R$ from $\widetilde E$ to $E$ that recovers the canonical purification. If Alice and Bob run the same admitted protocol and Eve retains her purification and the full transcript, $\mathcal R$ acting on the purifying register and the identity acting on the transcript recover the canonical output of Lemma 13. Moreover this channel maps every ideal secret-bit law with Eve in $\widetilde E T$ to an ideal secret-bit law with Eve in $ET$.

Consider inputs $\omega^{\otimes n}$ with $\omega\in\mathscr C$ and $n\ge1$, and admitted protocols whose normalized completed outputs retain in Eve’s register an arbitrary initial purification and the complete public transcript. The following statements extend the gap in Theorem 17; in item 2, the completed local output alphabet may include an abort symbol.* 1. *If $A$ is a measurable event of the complete public transcript with probability $r>0$, the normalized bit output conditioned on $A$ has distance at least $1/5$ from every ideal bit law for that accepted output. This holds for every $r>0$.* 2. *Suppose a sequence of completed protocols has a locally available abort symbol at either party. If the probability that at least one party aborts tends to zero, and the normalized non-aborting outputs approach ideal non-aborting bit laws, then replacing each local abort by the fixed bit zero would give completed bit outputs approaching ideal bits. Such a sequence is impossible for inputs in $\mathscr C$ (including any numbers of copies).* 3. *Let $\tau_k$ be completed normalized bit outputs to which the gap applies, possibly on different output spaces. Suppose their bit registers are kept fixed and their Eve registers are embedded in a common output space $F$, giving states $\widehat\tau_k$. The embeddings must preserve and permit recovery of the full initial purification and complete public records, without coarse-graining those records. In particular, an Eve-side recovery channel recovers $\tau_k$ from $\widehat\tau_k$ while leaving the bits fixed. If $\widehat\tau_k\to\tau$ in trace norm, then for every normalized law $\sigma_F$, $$\left\lVert\tau-\tfrac 12\sum_{i=0}^1 |i,i\rangle\langle i,i|\otimes\sigma_F\right\rVert_1\ge\frac15.$$

Let $L:M_{4}(\mathbb C)\to M_{4}(\mathbb C)$ be PPT. Suppose that $\mathcal X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_{20}\}\subset\mathbb C^4\setminus\{0\}$ represents twenty distinct projective directions and has the following properties:*

1.  *$\operatorname{rank}L(P_x)<4$ for every $x\in\mathcal X$, and every nonzero homogeneous quadratic in $\mathbb C[x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3]$ vanishes on at most nine members of $\mathcal X$;*

2.  *$L(P_y)$ is positive definite for some $y\in\mathbb C^4$.*

*Then there are PPT maps $\Phi_1,\Phi_2:M_{10}(\mathbb C)\to M_{10}(\mathbb C)$, constructed explicitly from $L$, such that $$Z=J(\Phi_2\circ\Phi_1)\ne0,\qquad
 \operatorname{ran}Z\cap\{u\otimes v:u,v\in\mathbb C^{10}\}=\{0\}.$$ In particular, $\Phi_2\circ\Phi_1$ is not entanglement breaking.

The map $L:M_{4}(\mathbb C)\to M_{4}(\mathbb C)$ in [eq:L] is PPT. For every $x\in\mathbb C^4$, $$L(P_x)=M(x)^{\mathsf T}\overline{M(x)}=M(x)^*M(x),\qquad \operatorname{rank}L(P_x)=\operatorname{rank}M(x). \label{eq:gram-identity}$$ Moreover, $L(P_{e_0})=36I_4$.

The projective directions $[x]\in\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ for which $\operatorname{rank}M(x)<4$ consist of exactly twenty distinct points. Each has a unique representative $x=(1,t_1,t_2,t_3)$. Every nonzero homogeneous quadratic in $\mathbb C[x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3]$ vanishes on at most nine of these representatives.
Any six complex bilinear forms on $\mathbb C^4\times\mathbb C^4$ have a common zero $(x,y)$ with $x\ne0$ and $y\ne0$.

Let $p$ be a prime, and let the coefficient field and its valuation ring be one of the pairs $$(\mathbb L,R_p)=(\mathbb Q,\mathbb Z_{(p)})
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 (\mathbb L,R_p)=(\mathbb Q_p,\mathbb Z_p).$$ If a monic polynomial $P\in R_p[z]$ factors as $P=gh$ with monic $g,h\in\mathbb L[z]$, then $g,h\in R_p[z]$, and their reductions modulo $p$ retain their degrees, including degree zero. Consequently, if $P$ has positive degree and irreducible reduction in $\mathbb F_p[z]$, then $P$ is irreducible over $\mathbb L$.

Let $F\in\mathbb Q[z]$ be monic, separable, and of positive degree, with coefficients in $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$. If its reduction in $\mathbb F_p[z]$ is squarefree with irreducible-factor degrees $s_1,\ldots,s_h$, then the Galois group of its rational splitting field contains an element with cycle lengths $s_1,\ldots,s_h$ on the roots.
If $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal U$ contains no two distinct sets whose associated vectors are orthogonal, then $|\mathcal F|\leq a_0=\delta b$.

For $t=1,2,3$, associate to $(A_1,\ldots,A_t)\in\mathcal U^t$ the unit vector $s_{A_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes s_{A_t}$. If $\mathcal R\subseteq\mathcal U^t$ contains no collection of $2^t$ distinct tuples whose associated vectors are pairwise orthogonal, then $$|\mathcal R|\leq t\delta b^t.$$

There is no choice of one projection from each of the six measurements in [eq:combinatorial-context-projections] such that the trace overlap of every two chosen projections from distinct contexts is strictly positive.
The vectors [eq:combinatorial-questions] and measurements [eq:combinatorial-global-projections] satisfy the two hypotheses of Proposition 26 with $n=m=QD$ and $\kappa=3a_0b^2

Set $$\label{eq:combinatorial-exact-data} \begin{gathered} p=257,\qquad k=1028,\qquad b=\binom{1027}{513},\qquad a_0=\sum_{j=0}^{256}\binom{1028}{j},\\ Q=b^3,\qquad K=1086373952,\qquad \kappa=3a_0b^2<\frac QK,\\ L=\binom Q8,\qquad D=4^L,\qquad m=QD. \end{gathered}$$ Use the vectors in [eq:combinatorial-questions], the $D$ labels per question and projections in [eq:combinatorial-global-projections], and the map $\Psi:M_{m}(\mathbb C)\to M_{D}(\mathbb C)$ in [eq:projection-map]. Put $\Lambda=\Psi^\dagger$ and $\Phi_D=\Omega_D/\sqrt D$.* 1. *The map $\Lambda/Q:M_{D}(\mathbb C)\to M_{m}(\mathbb C)$ is a trace-preserving PPT channel, and $$\label{eq:combinatorial-state} \rho_{\mathrm{comb}} =\left(\frac{\Lambda}{Q}\otimes\frac{\Lambda}{Q}\right) (\Phi_D\Phi_D^*) =\frac{J(\Psi^\dagger\circ\Psi)}{Q^2D}$$ is an entangled density operator on $\mathbb C^m\otimes\mathbb C^m$ belonging to $\mathscr C$. It has $K_D(\rho_{\mathrm{comb}})=0$ and satisfies the uniform unhalved $1/5$ gap and all operational consequences of Theorem 17 and Proposition 18, with their stated protocol, purification, and completion hypotheses.* 2. *For the real coordinate isometry $U:\mathbb C^D\to\mathbb C^m$ onto the first $D$ coordinates, the maps $$\Phi_1^{\mathrm{comb}}=\operatorname{Ad}_U\circ\Psi,\qquad \Phi_2^{\mathrm{comb}}=\Lambda\circ\operatorname{Ad}_{U^*} =(\Phi_1^{\mathrm{comb}})^\dagger$$ are PPT maps on $M_{m}(\mathbb C)$, and $$\label{eq:combinatorial-pair} J(\Phi_2^{\mathrm{comb}}\circ\Phi_1^{\mathrm{comb}}) =Q^2D\,\rho_{\mathrm{comb}}$$ is nonseparable over $\mathbb C^m\otimes\mathbb C^m$. In particular their composition is not entanglement breaking.* 3. *Let $\Theta_{\mathrm{comb}}$ be the channel obtained by applying Proposition 25 to this square pair. It is a trace-preserving PPT channel on $M_{2m+1}(\mathbb C)$. With the positive constants $c_1,c_2$ and the first coordinate inclusion $W_0$ from that proposition, the Choi matrix of its square has the corner $$\label{eq:combinatorial-channel-corner} (W_0^*\otimes W_0^*)J(\Theta_{\mathrm{comb}}^2) (W_0\otimes W_0) =c_1c_2Q^2D\,\rho_{\mathrm{comb}}.$$ Consequently $\Theta_{\mathrm{comb}}^2 =\Theta_{\mathrm{comb}}\circ\Theta_{\mathrm{comb}}$ is not entanglement breaking.
